assertion.statement: The local GI(k) hypothesis required by GT Proposition10.1 is available at k=r-1 and threshold min(alpha*delta/(4*Cstar),1/2), with fixed finite linear models independent of L,z,b and the ray-class union.
assertion.objects: The absolute one-bounded GI input in Proposition10.1; its relative real input is treated by that proposition, not inserted directly into the one-bounded theorem.
assertion.hypotheses: Fix the desired s>=2, r=max(s,4), k=r-1, Cstar and majorant scaling alpha before the norm threshold delta; the separate relative proposition requires its pseudorandom majorant.
assertion.quantifiers: For every fixed k and delta, all positive N and all such f; all orbit parameters allowed.
assertion.parameter_range: Each fixed r>=4 and k=r-1>=3; alpha>0,Cstar fixed; positive threshold at most1/2.
assertion.uniformity: Family, Lipschitz and correlation bounds are independent of N, f and orbit parameters.
assertion.constants: Finite C(k,delta), positive c(k,delta); no numerical/effective bound is claimed.
assertion.normalizations: The local theorem uses normalized interval Gowers norm. The current proof first converts the truncated relative input to the required U^r threshold using the exact indicator ratios.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No assertion that the prime-dominated relative input is one-bounded; no fixed-z pseudorandom limit or direct contradiction before the slow cutoff.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the finite-order parameters and threshold; apply the finite-family GI hypothesis inside the relative inverse theorem; the following stagewise cutoff separately supplies a sequence satisfying its asymptotic hypotheses.
